newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Standard Bank in one billion rand outsourcing deal.
newsitem.headline: Standard Bank in one billion rand outsourcing deal.

text.p: Standard Bank Corp said on Tuesday its card division had appointed Electronic Data Systems (EDS) to restructure, upgrade and manage its operational process in a 10-year outsourcing deal worth more than one billion rand.
Standard's card division assistant general manager Peter Abbott said: "The deal will enable the bank to provide its more than one million card holders with services on par with the best worldwide."
Abbott said a central component of the new arrangement was the transfer of around 430 card division employees to EDS. However, the move would involve no job losses at Standard Bank.
Abbott said that the one billion rand was not a capital investment and funds would flow into the deal over 10 years.
"This is not a capital investment, funds will flow over a 10 year period," he said.

In terms of the agreement, EDS would provide two key services: the re-engineering and ongoing delivery of Standard Bank card division's business activities and the implementation of the latest information technology needed to drive the new processes.
EDS Africa managing director James Fitzgerald said Standard would be getting direct access to the best global expertise.
"The improvements will be seen in the standard of products delivered to cardholders and in the supply of information to clients," he said.
Abbott emphasised that Standard would still be running the card division but that it had outsourced certain of the work.
"EDS will be bringing its international expertise to assist in operating the computer operations," he said.

He said outsourcing -- a process whereby a company hands out responsibility of certain of its services to an outside firm -- was an international trend and while Standard was the only bank so far to have entered into an outsourcing deal, he was sure other banks would soon follow suit.
EDS is the world's largest information technology services company, operating in 42 countries with a turnover of 12.4 billion U.S. dollars last year.
EDS Africa was established in March 1995 and is jointly owned by EDC, information technology group Dimension Data Holdings and chemicals and plastics producer AECI Ltd.
